title: Vasquez clears Holcot, Durandus, and Pico: they still required embrace and kiss—calling refusal to adore images in any way an intolerable crime
source_text: XXXIV. Ab eo vero, ut putat, errore Vasquez ibidem vindicat Holcot, Durandum, & Picum Mirandulanum, quos ostendit non negavisse amplexari nos debere imagines, salutare & osculari, atque ipsis caput nudare; etiamsi dixerint imagines per hoc improprie tantum adorari, & illam non esse proprie adorationem imaginis, sed exemplaris. Quapropter in fine capitis secundi modo citatae disputationis, affirmat scelus & crimen esse imagines non adorare, & errorem intolerabilem judicari debere, si quis doceat eas nullo modo esse adorandas.
pass_a_gloss: But from that error, as he thinks, Vasquez in the same place vindicates Holcot, Durandus, and Pico of Mirandola, whom he shows not to have denied that we ought to embrace images, salute and kiss them, and uncover the head to them; even if they said that by this images are only improperly adored, and that that is not properly the adoration of the image but of the exemplar. Wherefore at the end of the second chapter of the disputation just cited he affirms that it is a crime and a wickedness not to adore images, and that it ought to be judged an intolerable error if anyone teaches that they are in no way to be adored.
pass_b_english: Holcot, Durandus, and Pico, on Vasquez’s reading, still required kiss and bare head—even if they called it improper adoration of the image.
Vasquez: to teach images must not be adored at all is crime and intolerable error.
